fields.notes: Of Advaita's branch, his close servant who kept the accounts of his household (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 12.28). From Purī he wrote to King Pratāparudra that Advaita was the Lord and asked for 300 rupees to pay Advaita's debt; the Lord, displeased, kept him away until Advaita pleaded, and then told him never to take a king's money (Ādi 12.29-52).

Once a disciple of Advaita Ācārya; with Āgala Pāgala and Śaṅkara he would not give up jñāna when Advaita preached bhakti as the highest, and was rejected by him and put out of the Gauḍīya community (Prema-vilāsa 24; Advaita-prakāśa 20).

fields.name: Kāmadeva Paṇḍita
fields.notes: Disciple of Advaita Ācārya; a rāḍhī kulīna brāhmaṇa of Khaḍadaha. Married Rādhārāṇī, daughter of Kamalākara Pippalāi. Through his efforts Nityānanda came to live at Khaḍadaha. His great-grandson Cāṅdaśarmā installed Śrī Śrī Rādhākānta at Khaḍadaha (Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna).

Of Advaita's branch (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 12.58); at the Kheturī festival (Bhakti-ratnākara 10.403). There were two Viṣṇudāsa Ācāryas: from one descend the vārendra Gosvāmīs of Māṇikyaḍihi (he wrote the Sītā-guṇa-kadamba), from the other the rāḍhī Gosvāmīs of Kāndikhāli (Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna).

Not Viṣṇudāsa Ācārya of Nityānanda's branch, brother of Nandana Ācārya (his own record since 05-11-2026).

Of Advaita's branch (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 12.56). Family priest of Hiraṇya and Govardhana Majumdār of Saptagrāma and dīkṣā guru of Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī (Antya 6.161-162).

Not Yadunandana Ācārya of Jhāmaṭapura, disciple and father-in-law of Vīrabhadra (#1773).

A disciple of Advaita Ācārya, rejected by him for holding to jñāna rather than bhakti, with Kāmadeva Nāgara and Āgala Pāgala (Prema-vilāsa 24; Advaita-prakāśa 20).

One Assamese book (Gaurāṅga-sevaka, 1923) identifies him with the son of Kusumvar Bhuiyan and Satyasandhā of Bardoā, Naogaon (Assam), who died in 1489 Śaka at 111 — the parents and birthplace of Śrīmanta Śaṅkaradeva of Assam.
